Indicator: Labour Force Participation Rate, Age 15 Years and Above (%)
Definitions: The labour force is defined as all persons aged 15 years and above who are either employed (engaged in economic activity) or unemployed but actively seeking or available for work. The Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) represents the proportion of this labour force in relation to the total population of the same age group. The LFPR is estimated using the Usual Status (PS+SS) approach, which combines information from Principal Status (PS) and Subsidiary Status (SS) to reflect an individual’s usual activity status over a reference year. Estimates are reported for the total population as well as by gender (male/female) and by place of residence (rural/urban).

Indicator: Percentage Distribution of Female Workers By Employment Status, Casual Labour (%)
Definitions: This indicator represents the proportion of female workers who are employed as casual labourers within the labour force. Casual labour refers to individuals, particularly women in this context, who are employed on a non-regular basis in either farm or non-farm enterprises, including both household-run and non-household businesses. These workers are compensated according to the specific terms of a short-term or day-to-day work agreement, rather than receiving a fixed or continuous salary, and is reported as a share of the total female labour force.

Indicator: Percentage Distribution of Female Workers By Employment Status, Regular Wage/Salary (%)
Definitions: This indicator represents the proportion of female workers who are employed as regular wage or salaried employees within the labour force. Regular wage/salaried workers are individuals engaged in the farm or non-farm enterprises of others whether household-based or non-household enterprises and who receive wages or salaries on a recurring basis. Unlike casual labourers, their employment is not contingent on daily or short-term renewals of work contracts. This category includes workers who are paid by time (such as monthly or weekly salaries), those compensated by piece-rate wages, as well as paid apprentices engaged either full-time or part-time, and is reported as a share of the total female labour force.

Indicator: Percentage Distribution of Female Workers By Employment Status, Self-employed (%)
Definitions: This indicator measures the percentage of female workers who are engaged in self-employment within the labour force. Self-employed workers are those who operate their own farm or non-farm enterprises, or pursue a trade or profession independently, either on their own account or in partnership with a small number of others. This measure captures the extent to which female workers are engaged in self-directed and independent economic activity, as opposed to wage or casual employment, and is reported as a share of the total female labour force.

Indicator: Urban Population (in '000s)
Data Source: Census; Population Projections for Indian States 2011-2036
Definitions: The urban population refers to the number of people (in thousands) residing in areas classified as urban by the Census of India. Urban areas include all statutory towns, which are places with a municipal corporation, municipal council, cantonment board, or notified town area committee. They also include census towns, defined as settlements that meet three key criteria: (i) a minimum population of 5,000; (ii) at least 75% of the male working population engaged in non-agricultural activities; and (iii) a population density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre. In addition, certain contiguous areas adjoining a core town with a population of 50,000 or more may also be classified as urban, if they are highly likely to undergo urbanisation.
